The story relies heavily on subtext, which feels completely natural and enriches both the emotional depth and the setting of the piece. Because Anton is married and their time at the residency is ending, the two characters never explicitly state their romantic feelings for one another; instead, their attraction and the melancholy of their impending separation are communicated entirely through subtext. 

For example, during the flashback to the power cut, Marian brings a candle to Anton’s room. On the surface, they are discussing light sources ("I have a torch." / "I know."), but the subtext is an unspoken invitation to intimacy and a gentle, mutual acknowledgment of the boundaries they ends up respecting. Similarly, at the end of the story, when Anton successfully navigates the roundabout and says, "Just in time," they are ostensibly talking about learning the local roads, but the subtext speaks to the tragedy of them finally figuring out how to be together right as they have to leave. 

This subtext also directly enriches the setting. The Irish coast, the secluded second beach, the ancient stone walls dividing the fields, and the rising tide all mirror the characters' internal states. The tide coming in to erase their footprints on the hidden beach serves as a natural, unforced symbol for how their brief, unconsummated connection will soon be swallowed up by their regular lives, leaving "no sign" behind.
